<div id="catalogue-page"></div>

This page brings together the mobility datasets and fitted models available in
`nomad`. If you have a particular country in mind, you can start by finding its
datasets in the first table, then use the map to explore their coverage. The
model table and diagnostic plots further down the page show which models were
fit to those data and how well they reproduced the observed flows.

You can browse everything here without running any code. Each section also has
an expandable code panel if you would like to make the same tables or plots in
R, for example to restrict a comparison to the datasets relevant to your analysis.

## Mobility Data

The first table describes the source data. Alongside the country, it helps to
look at the spatial scale and collection dates, since these determine which
movements a model has been fit to explain. For example, movement between
large administrative areas may provide little information about short journeys
within a town. Expanding a row gives more detail on how the data were sampled
and whether flows below a reporting threshold were suppressed. Both can affect
the observed pattern of movement.

To find a dataset, type its name or country code in the search box, or click a
column heading to sort the table. The fitted-models column distinguishes entries
we can already use for prediction from datasets for which we currently hold only
metadata. Those entries remain in the table so that the catalogue also records
data that may become available later.

```{r datasets, fold_label="Show how to browse mobility datasets in R"}
datasets <- mobility_table()
reactable::reactable(
  datasets[, c("name", "country", "type", "n", "aggregation", "date_start",
                "date_end", "has_fitted_models")],
  searchable = TRUE, resizable = TRUE, wrap = FALSE,
  bordered = TRUE, highlight = TRUE,
  showPageSizeOptions = TRUE, pageSizeOptions = c(4, 8, 12, 24), defaultPageSize = 8,
  defaultSorted = list(date_start = "desc"),
  defaultColDef = reactable::colDef(minWidth = 100),
  theme = reactable::reactableTheme(highlightColor = "#eaf4f8"),
  columns = list(
    name = reactable::colDef(name = "Dataset", sticky = "left", minWidth = 175,
                             style = list(borderRight = "1px solid #ccd5da")),
    country = reactable::colDef(name = "ISO3", minWidth = 65),
    type = reactable::colDef(name = "Data", minWidth = 130),
    n = reactable::colDef(name = "Records", minWidth = 140, format = reactable::colFormat(digits = 0, separators = TRUE)),
    aggregation = reactable::colDef(name = "Spatial scale"),
    date_start = reactable::colDef(name = "Start"),
    date_end = reactable::colDef(name = "End"),
    has_fitted_models = reactable::colDef(name = "Fitted models", minWidth = 140,
                                          cell = function(x) if (x) "Yes" else "Not yet")
  ),
  details = function(index) {
    row <- datasets[index, ]
    period <- if (is.na(row$prediction_period_days)) "Unknown" else
      paste(row$prediction_period_days, "days")
    htmltools::tags$div(style = "padding: 12px; white-space: normal;",
      htmltools::tags$p(htmltools::tags$b("Sampling: "), row$sampling_scheme),
      htmltools::tags$p(htmltools::tags$b("Censoring: "),
                        if (is.na(row$censoring)) "Not specified" else row$censoring),
      htmltools::tags$p(htmltools::tags$b("Prediction period: "), period),
      if (!is.na(row$publication)) htmltools::tags$a("Publication", href = row$publication)
    )
  }
)
```

The start and end dates refer to the collection window. They do not necessarily
tell us the period represented by a predicted trip count, particularly when the
matrix used for fitting is an average of repeated observations. You can see the prediction
period by expanding the dataset's row. Predictions from the newer Facebook
models represent trip counts over 21 days.

The catalogue can also include shared data and models whose source metadata are
incomplete. The Zambia Facebook and CDR models from 2020 are examples for which
the prediction period is unavailable. Keeping these models accessible allows us
to explore their movement patterns, but the missing period limits their use for
predicting trip totals over a particular duration. An unknown entry in the table
is therefore a reason to consider what information your analysis requires.

## Where are the data from?

The map gives an overview of where the catalogued data come from. Use the buttons
in the top right to switch between Facebook and call data records, then click a
country to see its dataset details. Where several datasets cover the same
country and source, the map displays the most recent one. You can find the
others in the table above.

Darker shading indicates a larger number of records. This helps show the scale
of each dataset, although it should not be interpreted as a direct comparison of
travel rates because the sampling methods, record definitions and collection
periods differ. For the newer Facebook datasets, the source-region selector also
adds the administrative centroids used in the model inputs. This lets you look
more closely at the spatial scale represented by a particular dataset.

```{r coverage-map, fold_label="Show how to make the coverage map in R"}
world <- rnaturalearth::ne_countries(scale = "medium", type = "map_units",
                                       returnclass = "sf")
locations <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "source_locations.rds", package = "nomad"))
map_data <- datasets[order(datasets$date_end, decreasing = TRUE, na.last = TRUE), ]
map_data <- map_data[!duplicated(paste(map_data$country, map_data$type)), ]
world$country <- world$iso_a3
world$country[world$country == "-99"] <- world$adm0_a3[world$country == "-99"]
coverage <- merge(world[, c("country", "name_long")], map_data, by = "country")
coverage$log_records <- log10(coverage$n)
coverage$popup <- paste0(
  "<b>", coverage$name_long, "</b><br>", coverage$name,
  "<br>", coverage$date_start, " to ", coverage$date_end,
  "<br>Records: ", format(round(coverage$n), big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE),
  "<br>Spatial scale: ", coverage$aggregation,
  "<br>Fitted models: ", ifelse(coverage$has_fitted_models, "available", "not yet available")
)
palette <- leaflet::colorBin("YlOrBr", domain = coverage$log_records, bins = 5)
map <- leaflet::leaflet(coverage, width = "100%", height = 550)
map <- leaflet::addMapPane(map, "land", zIndex = 200)
map <- leaflet::addPolygons(map, data = world,
  color = "#bdc8cc", weight = 0.5, fillColor = "#f7f7f2", fillOpacity = 1,
  options = leaflet::pathOptions(pane = "land", interactive = FALSE,
    attribution = 'Boundaries: <a href="https://www.naturalearthdata.com/">Natural Earth</a>'))
for (source in c("facebook", "call data record")) {
  layer <- coverage[coverage$type == source, ]
  group <- if (source == "facebook") "Facebook" else "Call data records"
  map <- leaflet::addPolygons(map, data = layer, group = group,
    fillColor = ~palette(log_records), fillOpacity = 0.75,
    color = "#8c949b", weight = 1, popup = ~popup, label = ~name_long,
    highlightOptions = leaflet::highlightOptions(weight = 3, color = "#2c3e50",
                                                  bringToFront = TRUE))
}
map <- leaflet::addLayersControl(map, baseGroups = c("Facebook", "Call data records"),
                                 options = leaflet::layersControlOptions(collapsed = FALSE))
map <- leaflet::hideGroup(map, "Call data records")
map <- leaflet::addLegend(map, pal = palette, values = ~log_records,
                          title = "Records (log10)", position = "bottomleft")
ids <- sort(unique(locations$data_name))
for (id in ids) {
  points <- locations[locations$data_name == id, ]
  map <- leaflet::addCircleMarkers(map, data = points, lng = ~lon, lat = ~lat,
    radius = 3, color = "#2166ac", fillOpacity = 0.85, group = id,
    popup = ~htmltools::htmlEscape(label))
}
map <- leaflet::hideGroup(map, ids)
map <- leaflet::fitBounds(map, lng1 = -26, lat1 = -36, lng2 = 63, lat2 = 39)
htmlwidgets::onRender(map, '
function(el, x, ids) {
  var map = this;
  var control = L.control({position: "topright"});
  control.onAdd = function() {
    var label = L.DomUtil.create("label");
    label.style.cssText = "background: white; padding: 8px; border-radius: 4px";
    label.textContent = "Source regions: ";
    var select = document.createElement("select");
    select.setAttribute("aria-label", "Source dataset");
    var none = document.createElement("option");
    none.value = ""; none.textContent = "Country coverage";
    select.appendChild(none);
    ids.forEach(function(id) {
      var option = document.createElement("option");
      option.value = id; option.textContent = id;
      select.appendChild(option);
    });
    select.onchange = function() {
      ids.forEach(function(id) {
        var group = map.layerManager.getLayerGroup(id);
        if (group) map.removeLayer(group);
      });
      var selected = map.layerManager.getLayerGroup(select.value);
      if (selected && select.value) {
        map.addLayer(selected);
        map.fitBounds(L.featureGroup(selected.getLayers()).getBounds());
      } else {
        map.fitBounds([[-36, -26], [39, 63]]);
      }
    };
    label.appendChild(select);
    L.DomEvent.disableClickPropagation(label);
    L.DomEvent.disableScrollPropagation(label);
    return label;
  };
  control.addTo(map);
}', data = ids)
```

## Model Performance

Once you have identified a source dataset, use its name to find the corresponding
fits in the model table. You can also filter the columns by country, model family
or type. Clicking a fit statistic sorts the table, which is useful for comparing
models fit to the same observations.

The error measures need to be interpreted in relation to those observations.
A small RMSE for a dataset with relatively few trips does not demonstrate a
better model than a larger RMSE for a dataset with much higher counts. It is
therefore helpful to narrow the table to one dataset before comparing fit errors,
and then inspect the plots below to understand which flows each model misses.
Some statistics were not supplied for every fit. In particular, missing values
for the deviance information criterion (DIC) mean that those models cannot be
included when calculating weights from that statistic.

```{r fitted-models, fold_label="Show how to compare fitted models in R"}
models <- model_table()
reactable::reactable(
  models[, c("name", "country", "mobility_model", "model_type", "RMSE", "MAPE",
              "R2", "DIC", "max_rhat", "supports_newdata")],
  searchable = TRUE, filterable = TRUE, resizable = TRUE, wrap = FALSE,
  bordered = TRUE, highlight = TRUE,
  defaultSorted = list(R2 = "desc"),
  showPageSizeOptions = TRUE, pageSizeOptions = c(4, 8, 12, 24), defaultPageSize = 8,
  theme = reactable::reactableTheme(highlightColor = "#eaf4f8"),
  defaultColDef = reactable::colDef(minWidth = 90),
  columns = list(
    name = reactable::colDef(name = "Model", sticky = "left", minWidth = 260,
                             style = list(borderRight = "1px solid #ccd5da")),
    country = reactable::colDef(name = "ISO3", minWidth = 65),
    mobility_model = reactable::colDef(name = "Family", minWidth = 150),
    model_type = reactable::colDef(name = "Type", minWidth = 120),
    RMSE = reactable::colDef(format = reactable::colFormat(digits = 1, separators = TRUE)),
    MAPE = reactable::colDef(format = reactable::colFormat(digits = 2)),
    R2 = reactable::colDef(format = reactable::colFormat(digits = 3)),
    DIC = reactable::colDef(format = reactable::colFormat(digits = 0, separators = TRUE)),
    max_rhat = reactable::colDef(name = "Max R-hat"),
    supports_newdata = reactable::colDef(name = "New regions", minWidth = 100)
  )
)
```

The maximum R-hat column summarises a different aspect of the fit. R-hat compares
variation within and between sampling chains, so a high value suggests that the
chains have not adequately explored the same parameter distribution. Those fits
need further convergence review before relying on their parameter estimates.
A value close to one is encouraging, but you should also inspect the
parameter-level summaries available through `summary(model)` and consider whether
the source data suit your application.

The final column indicates whether a model can predict for new regions. Basic
and finite radiation models are restricted to their original regions and
populations, even when their stored fit statistics look favourable. Other model
families can be applied to new inputs, with checks and warnings described in the
[model selection vignette](selecting-a-model.html).

## Model Fit Checks

Choose a model from the dropdown to inspect its saved diagnostic plot. The first
panel compares observed and predicted flows, while the residual panel shows the
differences between them. For example, a model may reproduce the largest flows
reasonably well but consistently miss smaller ones. Such a pattern can matter
for an analysis of how infection reaches less connected regions, even when the
overall error appears small.

These plots describe agreement with the data used to fit each model. They help
us understand that fit, but do not tell us how well it will predict movement in
a different place or period. The code below the plot shows how to retrieve the
same checks and parameter summaries for a selected model in R.

```{r gallery-assets, include=FALSE}
plot_dir <- "model_checks"
dir.create(plot_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
for (id in names(model_db)) {
  source <- nomad:::check_plot_file_path(model_db[[id]])
  destination <- file.path(plot_dir, paste0(id, ".png"))
  if (file.exists(source)) {
    file.copy(source, destination, overwrite = TRUE)
  } else {
    grDevices::png(destination, width = 1200, height = 600, res = 150)
    plot(model_db[[id]])
    grDevices::dev.off()
  }
}
```

```{r gallery, echo=FALSE, results="asis"}
selected <- "zmb_fb_2025_mod_grav_exp_norm"
options <- lapply(names(model_db), function(id) {
  htmltools::tags$option(value = id, selected = if (id == selected) "selected" else NULL, id)
})
htmltools::tags$div(
  htmltools::tags$label("Model: ", `for` = "plotSelect"),
  htmltools::tags$select(id = "plotSelect", style = "max-width:100%; margin-bottom:1em;",
    onchange = "document.getElementById('plotImage').src = 'model_checks/' + this.value + '.png'; document.getElementById('plotImage').alt = 'Fit diagnostics for ' + this.value;",
    options),
  htmltools::tags$img(id = "plotImage", class = "catalogue-plot",
    src = paste0("model_checks/", selected, ".png"),
    alt = paste("Fit diagnostics for", selected))
)
```

```{r fit-in-r, eval=FALSE, fold_label="Show how to inspect the same fit in R"}
model <- model_db$zmb_fb_2025_mod_grav_exp_norm
check(model, plots = FALSE)
plot(model)
summary(model)
```

comparison of predictions, uncertainty and ensembles.
